problems: Exposes internal seat roles and internal skill names to a public reader.
Claims 'Live' while one seat sits in error.
No artefact a hiring manager can read; the diagram file path is printed as text.
projects.lede: Nine agents, one operating picture. Each seat owns a function, reports upward, and cannot act outside its role. The interesting problem was not building an agent; it was stopping nine of them from becoming nine separate systems.
how: Every seat has a written contract: what it owns, what it may touch, who it reports to.
Work enters through a single queue and is routed down one chain, so two agents cannot quietly take the same job.
Every model change and every dispatch rule is a decision on record, not a setting someone remembers.
Health is read from the live roster, not from the last status message.
projects.contribution: Role design, the routing and dispatch rules, model allocation across seats, and the board the whole fleet runs on.
projects.verified: Nine seats live at audit time. Fleet is coordinated through one issue board. One seat was in an error state on the day of the audit, which is why the status is Running with a caveat rather than Live.
projects.limits: Not an autonomous company: a human still holds every irreversible decision. No public metric exists for throughput or cost per task, so none is claimed.
projects.seo: Agent Fleet — Coordinating Nine AI Agents as One System | Raqeeb Hussain
projects.meta: How nine AI agents are coordinated as one governed system: written role contracts, a single routing chain, and live roster health instead of status messages.

projects.eyebrow: PROCEDURAL MEMORY · REUSABLE AGENT SKILLS · RUNNING
problems: 'Triple-provenance model' and 'curator hygiene' are internal jargon a hiring manager cannot parse.
The value of the work (repeating a procedure exactly) is never stated.
projects.lede: A prompt is a one-off. A skill is a procedure the agent can repeat on Tuesday without being reminded. This library is how the same standard survives across agents and sessions.
how: Each skill is a single file: when to use it, what to do, the commands that work, and the mistakes to avoid.
Skills are versioned in git, so a change to a procedure is a diff someone can review.
The same skill loads for every seat that needs it, so two agents do not invent two ways to do one job.
A maintenance skill tracks drift between the local copy and upstream.
projects.contribution: The authoring standard, the library itself, and the discipline that turns a repeated mistake into a written rule.
projects.verified: 438 skill packages present on the machine at audit time, plus 315 workflow skill packages from the orchestration layer.
projects.limits: Quality varies by skill; a written procedure is only as good as the last time it was tested. No benchmark exists for skill effectiveness, so none is claimed.
projects.seo: Skills Library — Reusable Agent Procedures | Raqeeb Hussain
projects.meta: Why reusable, versioned agent skills beat one-off prompts: when to use, what to do, commands that work, and the mistakes to avoid, in one file.

problems: Undefined operational terms: MDD and reconciliation mean nothing to a hiring manager outside drilling.
The site implies live delivery; email, OneDrive and Telegram are blocked stubs in the repository.
Posters and two real demo videos exist but the page still says 'video coming soon'.
projects.lede: A drilling services operator tracks equipment by rig, by well and by job cycle. When those three drift apart, the invoice and the field report disagree and someone spends a day reconciling. This console makes the drift visible before it becomes a dispute.
how: A job's identity is rig plus well plus job cycle, never the rig alone, so the same rig on two wells never merges into one record.
Field paperwork is ingested and matched against the tracking record; mismatches surface as an exception instead of being averaged away.
Material delivery documents are checked against the same record before anything is accepted.
A daily digest gives the operator the state of the day without opening five files.
A separate track reads morning reports for competitor tool sizes and company activity, labelled as market observation, never as an operational claim.
projects.contribution: Console design and build, the reconciliation logic, the per-client workspace, and the ingest pipeline.
projects.verified: Repository README (2026-10-20): operations and market intelligence tracks, local SQLite per client, client-scoped API. Two demo videos and the interactive diagrams are on disk.
projects.limits: Demo-local by design: approving an action mutates demo state only, and email, OneDrive and Telegram are blocked stubs that refuse to deliver. No production client data is in the repository.
projects.seo: OrIO Operations — Drilling Operations Console | Raqeeb Hussain
projects.meta: Operations console for a drilling services pilot: rig, well and job-cycle tracking, document reconciliation, exception handling, and a separate market intelligence track.

problems: Claims 'official commercial registry validation' when registry lookup is an optional stage that needs a known CR number.
Claims a Twenty CRM GraphQL integration that does not exist in the code.
Never says the system runs on a local model with no paid key.
projects.lede: Saudi B2B lead generation has a trust problem: lists are cheap, verified contacts are not. LeadJin finds companies, finds the people inside them, verifies both, and refuses to send to anyone it cannot show a source for.
how: Discovery runs as a waterfall: cache, then places data, then optional registry lookup where a CR is known, then the preserved legacy engines, then the local model. A stage that cannot run says so instead of returning an empty list.
People are found on company pages, social bios and public profiles through indexed search, never through a logged-in scrape.
Every contact is checked before it is used: mail server records first, then a real handshake, with the evidence and timestamp stored.
Sending is constrained by rule: a discovered contact needs recorded consent, the cadence is exactly three emails, and every message carries a real sender identity and an opt-out.
projects.contribution: Product definition, the pipeline, the verification rules, the sending rules, the interface, and the local model wiring.
projects.verified: Running locally at audit time: service on port 3001, health ok, local model gemma4:e4b over Ollama, decision service on port 8020. Company dataset of 6,701 records, 6,568 of them licence-cleared. Harvest returns leads, and the working database holds a real outreach history.
projects.limits: Pilot, not production. Registry lookup is optional and needs a known CR. Places returns no email and no people, so contact harvesting is the load-bearing step. No Twenty CRM integration exists; pipeline state lives in the product's own tables.
projects.seo: LeadJin — Verified KSA Lead Generation | Raqeeb Hussain
projects.meta: LeadJin: KSA lead discovery, contact harvesting, triple verification and consent-bound outreach, running locally on an open model with no paid API key.

problems: Describes 'cryptographic hash gating' and 'SiYuan state storage'; the repository states there is no SiYuan dependency.
Leaks the internal governance model into the stack list.
Does not say what a reviewer actually sees.
projects.lede: An agent that can publish, send or spend should not be able to do it alone. This inbox puts the artefact in front of a human, in the place the human already works, and makes the decision the thing that unblocks the action.
how: Work that needs a decision is submitted to one inbox with its artefact attached: an image, a carousel, a video, or a PDF.
The reviewer sees the artefact itself, not a description of it, and approves with a confirmation that names what is being released.
A rejection carries a reason that travels back to the owner of the work, so the next attempt knows what to change.
The decision wakes the working session, so approve executes exactly the next action shown and reject stops it. If no session is reachable, it falls back to a board card.
projects.contribution: Workflow design, the inbox interface, the submission and file-handling API, and the fail-closed rule for reaching a live session.
projects.verified: Repository README (main): single inbox, artifact previews, decision wakes the live session, opt-in injection flag that fails closed when unset. Plugin installed and enabled on this machine; live-session injection is currently off, so a decision records and creates a board card instead of reaching a session.
projects.limits: Live-session injection is opt-in and fails closed by default; without it a decision only records and creates a board card. No hash-chain audit trail exists, so none is claimed.
projects.seo: Approval Inbox — Human Review for AI Agent Actions | Raqeeb Hussain
projects.meta: An approval inbox that puts the artefact in front of a human before an agent acts: previews, named confirmations, reasons on rejection, and a fail-closed link to the working session.

projects.eyebrow: INTEGRATION · AGENT RUNTIME TO WORK BOARD · RUNNING
problems: Internal tool names with no explanation of the business problem.
Claims 'recovery-action disposition' without saying what fails and what recovers.
projects.lede: An agent is only useful if its work is visible somewhere a human already looks. This plugin connects the agent runtime to the company work board so a task is claimed, worked and closed in the same place it was assigned.
how: An agent checks out an issue before working on it, so two agents cannot start the same task.
Progress is reported back while the work runs, not only at the end.
Files produced by the run are attached to the issue, so the evidence lives with the task.
Failures are written back with their reason, so the next attempt starts from the real state.
projects.contribution: The integration layer between the runtime and the board, and the checkout, reporting and attachment behaviour.
projects.verified: Plugin installed and running; the board API answers with nine agents and a live issue set at audit time.
projects.limits: One board implementation. The plugin follows that API's shape, so a different work system would need its own adapter.
projects.seo: Paperclip Plugin — Wiring AI Agents Into a Work Board | Raqeeb Hussain
projects.meta: Integration layer that lets AI agents claim, report and close work on a company board, with attachments and failure reasons kept on the task.

projects.eyebrow: AGENT RUNTIME · CONFIGURATION AND EXTENSION · RUNNING
problems: 'Rule 0 gates and Step 0 pre-flight validation' is internal shorthand presented to outsiders.
The page never explains what an agent runtime actually does for a business.
projects.lede: An agent runtime is the difference between a chat window and a worker: a model, a set of tools, a memory, a schedule, and a place to record what happened. Most of my AI work starts here.
how: Each agent gets its own configuration: which model, which tools, which files it may touch.
Memory and session context are separated from authority, so a remembered fact cannot silently become a decision.
Tools are registered per plugin, so a new capability is an install, not a rewrite.
Every run leaves a record: what was asked, what was called, what came back.
projects.contribution: Runtime configuration, plugin integration, model routing, and the operating discipline that keeps runs reproducible.
projects.verified: This portfolio, the fleet, the skills library and the automation work all run on the configured runtime described here.
projects.limits: I configure and extend an open source runtime; I did not author its core. Model and tool behaviour changes between versions, which is why runs are recorded rather than remembered.
projects.seo: Agent Runtime Integration — Models, Tools, Memory | Raqeeb Hussain
projects.meta: What an agent runtime is and how it is configured: per-agent models and tools, memory separated from authority, plugin-registered capabilities and recorded runs.

problems: Claims '38+ autonomous cron workflows … zero human intervention'. The registry holds 47 jobs, all paused.
Status says Live. Nothing is scheduled right now.
No single workflow is described end to end, which is exactly what the brief asks for.
projects.lede: Automation is only worth building when the trigger, the input and the output are all known. These are the workflows I built, the shape each one takes, and their honest state today.
how: Trigger, input, processing, output, and the human step where one is required: every workflow is specified in those five parts before it is scheduled.
Each job records its own last run and last failure, so a silent stop is visible.
A digest job de-duplicates what it has already sent, so a repeat is not news.
A watch job compares an external surface against its last known state, and reports the change, not the state.
projects.contribution: Workflow design, the scheduling and triage discipline, and the failure handling.
projects.verified: 47 scheduled jobs exist in the registry. All 47 are paused, none is enabled, and none has a next run: the scheduler was stopped by decision, not by failure.
projects.limits: Paused. Nothing is running on a schedule today. Any page copy that says otherwise is wrong, and the fix is to show the state honestly.
projects.seo: Automation Workflows — Trigger, Input, Output | Raqeeb Hussain
projects.meta: How automated workflows are specified and run: trigger, input, processing, output and the human step, with the honest state of the current scheduler.
